text:
mike_su: Heads-up — AcmePay (dedicated customer) opened an escalation: widespread 429s starting ~08:14 UTC. They say token-level throttling despite having reserved capacity. I see requests landing in the wrong pool. Sample control-plane response and client error below.

mike_su: Client curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"acme-llama-70b","prompt":"hi"}'` -> 429 Too Many Requests

mike_su: Response headers: `x-redwood-pool: dedicated-us-west-2-small`, `x-request-tier: gold`, `x-routing-reason: tier_mismatch_fallback`

mike_su: Customer claims their reservation is for `dedicated-us-west-2-large` (500 QPS). We should not be falling back to small for gold-tier customers.

julia_sre: Looking. Can you paste the routing policy id from the control plane decision?

mike_su: Found `route_policy_id: rp-78f3-zz` in the decision blob. Also included the config snippet they use: `route_rules: [{match: {tags: {tier: "gold"}}, pool: "dedicated-us-west-2-large"}]`

raj_ops: I pulled the control-plane logs for rp-78f3. There's a bunch of entries like `match_evaluation: tags.tier == null` right before fallback. Seems the tag map parsing returned null for some requests.

devin_eng: Noted. Any pattern in client headers? Are they sending `tier` as a tag or as a label?

mike_su: Customer says their SDK attaches `tier=gold` in `x-redwood-tags: tier=gold,team=payments`. I can repro locally by sending `x-redwood-tags` exactly like that.

julia_sre: That header should be parsed into a map. If parsing fails we hit fallback which picks a smaller pool to satisfy SLOs. Can we reproduce routing logic locally?

devin_eng: Reproduced. If header contains `tier=gold` (no quotes), the parser returns a single string instead of a map in ~2% of requests due to a split-on-comma bug. When that happens, `tags.tier` lookup returns null and policy matcher falls through to fallback.

devin_eng: Repro steps: `for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H \"x-redwood-tags: tier=gold,team=payments\" ...; done` — saw ~18 429s with `x-redwood-pool: dedicated-us-west-2-small` and `routing-reason: tier_mismatch_fallback`.

raj_ops: Oof. That explains the noisy neighbor effect — small pool saturates and autoscaler doesn't spin because it's not the reserved one.

julia_sre: What's the minimal patch? Devin?

devin_eng: Patch is two lines: change split logic to `split(/,(?=(?:[^\"]*\"[^\"]*\")*[^\"]*$)/)` to avoid naive comma split inside quoted values, and fallback defensively to try parsing `key=value` pairs even if top-level parse failed. I opened PR: https://git.redwood/infra/rp-fix-parse/pull/12

deploy-bot: deploy started for infra/routing-parser v2026.03.17-rc2 -> rolling to control plane nodes (6 nodes)

mike_su: Did we confirm no other policy mismatches? Any other policies using tags parsing?

devin_eng: Grepped: 14 route policies use `x-redwood-tags` matching. Will run smoke across them.

billing-bot: FYI — flagged affected customer's billing: timestamps 08:14-09:00 showed high error rate; we will not bill for throttled tokens but note usage spikes in logs.

julia_sre: After deploy, can someone validate AcmePay traffic path? Mike, can you ask the customer to retry a couple of calls?

mike_su: Sent to AcmePay oncall with repro snippet and request to retry.

mike_su: Customer replied: after 2 retries, responses now show `x-redwood-pool: dedicated-us-west-2-large` and 200s. They report error rate dropped to normal.

devin_eng: Smoke passed for other policies. Adding unit test that reproduces the comma-in-quoted-value case. Also adding a small-run canary to control plane rollout.

raj_ops: I'll monitor autoscaler metrics for small pool to ensure it drains and large pool receives traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy completed for infra/routing-parser v2026.03.17-rc2 -> success on 6/6 nodes

julia_sre: Closing loop — root cause: tag header parsing edge-case (comma splitting bug) causing `tier` to be null -> policy fallthrough -> fallback to smaller pool -> customer throttled. Fix deployed and customer recovered.

mike_su: Marking as P1 resolved in support ticket. Will follow up with postmortem and patch ETA for full rollout (including integration tests). :white_check_mark:

devin_eng: PR merged to main, backporting to 2026.02 maintenance branch. Also created a synthetic test that fuzzes `x-redwood-tags` header parsing.

julia_sre: Good job team. Add remediation note: proactively scan route policies for header-dependent matchers and add defensive parsing.

mike_su: Thanks all. Closing thread.
